answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require verifiable proof-of-burn before issuing credentials. In automated swarms monitoring cedar reserves or raven habitats, each agent must provably destroy cryptocurrency to register a node. An attacker incurs a non-refundable financial loss per created identity, which makes mass spoofing cost-prohibitive. However, deep-pocketed adversaries can still harbor fraudulent nodes if the payoff of subverting the swarm exceeds the burned capital.
